pages.title: Categorical interpretation evaluation
text: **Categorical agreement depends on the applicable interpretation rules**

Categorical evaluation compares the investigational and reference interpretations within a defined organism–antimicrobial–method domain. It should use the applicable rule version and retain the underlying measurements. The same diameter can lead to different interpretations when the method or standards context changes. [R01] [R02]
## Use correct denominators

Categorical agreement is the proportion of evaluable paired results assigned the same category under the specified framework. For conventional error analyses, a very major error concerns an investigational susceptible result when the reference is resistant; its denominator is the relevant reference-resistant set. A major error concerns an investigational resistant result when the reference is susceptible, with the corresponding reference-susceptible denominator. Exact handling must follow the chosen evaluation framework.
## Do not merge unlike category meanings

EUCAST's I category denotes susceptibility with increased exposure; it should not be casually equated with another framework's intermediate category. The system should preserve the source vocabulary and any approved mapping rather than translating categories through a generic three-letter lookup.

The proposed evaluation should report measurement and interpretation errors separately where possible. A correct numerical measurement can still receive an incorrect category through a rule-mapping defect. Conversely, a measurement error may remain within the same category while exposing a weakness that matters near another threshold. Both patterns require investigation.

pages.title: Evaluating rare and consequential errors
text: **Zero observed errors do not establish a zero error rate**

Rare consequential errors require deliberate statistical planning. If n independent eligible cases produce zero errors, an exact one-sided 95% binomial upper bound for the underlying error probability is 1 − 0.05^(1/n). This is a mathematical illustration under independent, identically distributed Bernoulli assumptions, not a product performance result.
## Plan the relevant denominator

For a particular error class, the relevant sample may be only the reference-resistant or reference-susceptible subset, not every test in the study. Multiple drug results from one isolate may also be dependent. The analysis should reflect that structure rather than treating every output as an independent opportunity to demonstrate safety.

The zero-error ambition is translated into engineering requirements: prevent known failure sequences, detect disagreement, abstain when evidence is inadequate and recover without inventing data. Each control needs measurable performance, including false alarms and missed failures. Multiple sensors cannot guarantee zero error because common causes can make them agree incorrectly.
## Interpret the evidence conservatively

An enriched challenge collection can help investigate rare failure modes, while a representative workflow study helps estimate operational coverage. These designs answer different questions. A credible claim should state the assessed error class, domain, denominator and confidence interval. The absence of an observed error is encouraging evidence within that study, not proof that an error is impossible.

pages.title: Abstention and coverage evaluation
text: **Abstention is useful only when its cost and coverage are visible**

An abstaining system declines to produce an eligible result when evidence is insufficient. This can reduce unsafe outputs, but a model can achieve a low accepted-case error rate by rejecting most difficult cases. Evaluation must therefore report both accuracy among accepted cases and the proportion of the intended workload that receives a result.
## Proposed selective-performance report

The study should define eligibility independently of model confidence, then account for every eligible case. Reasons for abstention should be meaningful, such as unreadable image, identity uncertainty, unsupported domain or sensor disagreement. A generic failure category can conceal distinct problems requiring different remedies.
## Test thresholds on independent data

Confidence thresholds should be selected using permitted development data and evaluated after being fixed. Reporting the most favorable threshold from the final test set would bias the result. Performance should also be stratified by site, organism and relevant difficult conditions.

The proposed interface should offer a useful next step without disguising abstention as a negative result. “Unavailable because the boundary is unreadable” has different meaning from a measured diameter. A receiving system must preserve this distinction so that an abstained case is not accidentally converted into zero, susceptible or normal during export.

pages.title: Robustness to imaging disturbances
text: **Robustness testing should reproduce meaningful disturbances**

The imaging system should be challenged with disturbances expected within or near its operating limits. Relevant factors include glare, condensation, exposure variation, blur, plate pose, label occlusion, background changes and vessel variation. Tests should assess both measurement degradation and the ability to recognize an unsupported image.
## Separate tolerance from detection

Some disturbances may be small enough for qualified measurement to continue. Others should trigger abstention. The study should establish the boundary between these states and verify that the quality check recognizes it. A system that remains numerically stable on a visually corrupted image may be confidently wrong.
## Use physical and synthetic challenges appropriately

Synthetic perturbations can isolate a software property, while physical tests reveal interactions among optics, material and environment. A simulated blur filter may not reproduce all effects of an actual focus change. Both forms of evidence should state their scope.

The proposed report should identify the disturbance level, affected area and reference behavior. Combined disturbances deserve attention because several mild effects can jointly invalidate a measurement. Recovery tests should verify that a successful recapture produces a new linked observation and that the original failed image remains available for investigation.

pages.title: Sensor failure and common causes
text: **Multiple sensors can share the same failure**

Multimodal sensing can improve error detection when channels provide complementary information. It can also create false agreement when several channels share a calibration error, clock fault, power disturbance or confounding environment. The proposed validation should test the independence assumed by the fusion method.
## Build a common-cause map

The engineering team should identify shared power, timing, mounting, calibration, preprocessing and environmental dependencies. A fault in one shared element may affect many apparently separate measurements. Voting across those measurements does not create independent confirmation.
## Evaluate the recovery decision

Detection alone is insufficient. The system must choose an appropriate qualified fallback, request review or abstain. Excluding a faulty auxiliary sensor may be acceptable for one task and invalidate another. Reduced-input modes need separate evidence and explicit eligibility rules.

The study should report fault-specific detection, false alarms, detection delay and the correctness of the resulting workflow state. It should also include faults not represented during model training. AMReye.AI's error-reduction strategy is therefore a combination of diverse evidence, explicit dependency analysis and safe handling of uncertainty, with no guarantee that sensor multiplicity eliminates every error.

pages.title: Early result validation
text: **An early result must be evaluated at the claimed time**

Rapid-AST research should specify the clock origin, specimen context, organism–drug scope and reference method before evaluation. An early output is eligible only if the method and interpretation have been established for that time. Routine endpoint breakpoints are not automatically applicable to a shorter observation interval. [R04] [R05]
## Proposed sub-two-hour study definition

The study should state which preparations and observations occur within the two-hour interval and which occur beforehand. It should preserve timestamps for unsuccessful cases and include the time needed for mandatory review when the claim concerns a reviewed result.
## Preserve the time-to-result distribution

A median below two hours can coexist with many much later cases. Report the fraction meeting the target and the distribution of delays. A model should not be scored at its eventual successful time when the claim concerns an earlier fixed deadline.

The initial programme may focus on selected workflows where sufficient signal is plausible. Expansion to other organisms, drugs or specimens requires new evidence. External studies motivate these investigations, but their analytical speed and performance cannot be imported as an AMReye.AI result.

pages.title: Human review and usability validation
text: **Human review needs validation as part of the system**

The complete product includes the interaction between software and intended users. A correct algorithm can still lead to an incorrect result through confusing presentation, wrong-record selection or ineffective correction controls. Usability evaluation should focus on tasks whose failure could affect safety, data integrity or the laboratory decision.
## Proposed critical tasks

Users should be able to verify identity, recognize unreadable observations, inspect measurement context, resolve flags, correct a result and understand the consequences of approval. Simulation views add the task of distinguishing measured evidence from predicted continuation.
## Assess realistic conditions

Participants should represent intended users, and tasks should reflect workload, interruptions and available training. Assistance from the development team during a study can conceal interface weaknesses. Observed difficulties should be analyzed for their causes and addressed through design where feasible.

The evaluation should measure errors, recoveries and understanding as well as task duration. A faster interface that encourages automatic acceptance of uncertain outputs would not satisfy the review objective. The proposed release evidence should show that users can carry out critical tasks reliably within the product's intended context, with remaining limitations reflected in design, training and use restrictions.

pages.title: Software verification and release control
text: **Software verification should follow the consequences of failure**

Verification checks that software requirements are implemented correctly and that components interact as specified. The proposed development process should link requirements, risk controls, design and test evidence. Lifecycle standards such as IEC 62304 provide a relevant planning framework; applicability and classification require product-specific assessment. [R52]
## Test the complete result path

Unit checks can validate numerical functions and state transitions. Integration tests should verify identity, calibration, interpretation, review and export together. System tests should include interrupted operations and realistic failure states. Passing isolated algorithm tests does not establish a correct end-to-end record.
!FIG work/assets/figures/verification-layers.png | Proposed verification layers and the need to reassess evidence when the configuration changes.
## Control what changes after testing

A release should identify software, models, standards rules and relevant dependencies independently. If one changes, the affected evidence should be reassessed. A signed or integrity-checked package supports distribution control, but it does not establish that the contents are clinically correct.

The proposed release process should retain test failures and their resolution, known limitations and rollback instructions. Unresolved issues need a documented impact assessment. A development build, public demonstration and qualified product release should have distinct identities so that evidence or records from one cannot be mistaken for another.

pages.title: Standards content verification
text: **Standards content is a separately controlled product dependency**

The interpretation service should identify the standards body, document version, correction state and applicable method. Measurement algorithms and standards rules need independent version identities. Updating a model should not silently change clinical thresholds, and updating thresholds should not obscure the measurement originally produced. [R01] [R02]
## Proposed content verification

Authorized source material should be mapped into structured rules by a controlled process with expert review. Tests should cover organism and antimicrobial mappings, units, method restrictions, footnotes, unavailable combinations and correction notices. Licensed content should be handled under its applicable terms.
## Check boundary behavior deliberately

Test values at, immediately below and immediately above relevant thresholds, following the method's rounding and reporting conventions. Character encoding, decimal separators and unit conversion can produce defects even when the source table was read correctly.

The proposed release package should include a standards-content manifest and regression evidence. A language model may assist expert review but should not generate executable breakpoints from memory. Before deployment, the team must verify the current source version and corrections again, because a dated compendium cannot guarantee that its reference snapshot remains the applicable rule set indefinitely.

pages.title: Interoperability verification
text: **Interoperability is preservation of meaning across a boundary**

An interface can transmit data successfully while changing its meaning. A missing value converted to zero, a simulated result treated as measured or a corrected report handled as a duplicate can create serious downstream errors. Verification should test semantics, identity and workflow states as well as network delivery.
## Proposed interface contract

Each receiving system should have an approved mapping for identifiers, units, terminology, result states, timestamps and amendments. The mapping should state which information is mandatory and what happens when it is absent. A transport acknowledgment should not be mistaken for clinical acceptance or review.
## Test both sides of the exchange

A local export file that looks correct does not establish that the receiving system interpreted it correctly. End-to-end testing should include readback or equivalent confirmation of the stored meaning. The assessment should also cover retries, timeouts and partial failures.

The proposed platform should preserve the original export payload and mapping version where appropriate for audit and privacy requirements. Changes to a laboratory system or interface profile need impact assessment. Interoperability is a maintained service responsibility, not a one-time claim based on the presence of an API endpoint.

pages.title: Traceable audit and correction records
text: **An audit trail should explain a result's history**

The audit record should capture who performed a relevant action, what changed, when it occurred and which record versions were affected. It should distinguish user actions, automated processing and administrative operations. The purpose is to reconstruct the result pathway and investigate discrepancies without relying on recollection.
## Proposed event model

Events should use stable identifiers and reference the exact input and output versions. Original observations remain preserved. Corrections append a new state and reason, while dependent analyses and approvals are assessed for invalidation. Audit access itself should be controlled and monitored.
## Integrity and completeness are different

A cryptographic integrity check can reveal changed bytes, but it cannot prove that an event was recorded truthfully or that all relevant events exist. The system needs reliable event generation, durable storage, clock context and reconciliation of interrupted operations.

Verification should include attempts to bypass normal editing paths, interrupted writes and corrections after export. The resulting history should remain understandable to an authorized reviewer. Retention and deletion policies must also account for applicable legal and institutional requirements; “immutable” should describe controlled alteration behavior, not an unqualified promise to retain personal data forever.
